newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids flat to down again despite crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids flat to down again despite crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices again were unchanged to down slightly Thursday in light trade, with sluggish East Coast utility demand still weighing on the complex despite a recovery in crude, industry sources said.

"There's not much demand now, so I don't see much upside, but we could see some life if gas moves up a little more," said one cash trader, noting city gate gas prices gained 10 percent this month and made some fuel grades more attractive.
New York Harbor physical one percent again eased slightly to $14.75 a barrel, but May paper, which sold early at $14.40, changed hands later at $14.60, little changed from Wednesday.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was unchanged at $16.25, with barrels for mid-May delivery offered closer to $16.
Traders said despite softer East Coast city gate gas prices today, recent gains made switching to some higher sulphur grades more attractive.
High sulphurs in New York held relatively steady, with three percent still quoted at $14.00-25, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent slipped more than a quarter to $14.25-50, pressured by reports that 65,000 barrels of one percent for May 15 delivery sold late Wednesday at $14.05.
USG three percent eased slightly to $13.00-25, with May paper quoted at $13.25-50, traders said.

New York city gate swing gas prices skidded more than 10 cents Thursday to about $2.35-40/mmBtu, or $14.99 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, lost about a dime to the $2.10/mmBtu area, or $13.23 a barrel.
